chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Beware of quarrelling and disputing, for these two cause illness in the hearts towards the brothers, and upon them hypocrisy grows.'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and social consequences of quarrelling and disputing according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) that quarrelling (al-mira') and disputing (al-khusumah) are detrimental to social bonds, causing spiritual illness in the hearts towards fellow believers and fostering the growth of hypocrisy. This hadith, recorded in al-Kafi, highlights the psychological and spiritual decay caused by contentiousness, warning that persistent argumentation erodes sincerity and leads to nifaq (hypocrisy) within the community of believers.
